title: Ops Field 3x3 Battlecard Matrix (sketch)
content:
Purpose:
Quick, copy-ready slide set + pocket reference for SEs and field ops to triage pilot conversations. Focus is buyer-centered one-liners, deterministic checks, and operational fallbacks. This is a sketch: keep it low-friction for sellers to memorize and use during calls.

Slide 1 — TL;DR (speaker notes)
- Goal: reduce pilot friction by giving SEs a 9-cell cheat matrix mapping persona x risk -> immediate response + demo cue + canary metric.
- How to use: open during intro (first 10m) and drop the one-liner and demo cue; keep the canary metric as acceptance criteria for post-call follow-up.
- Audience: SEs, Sales Ops, Customer Success onboarding engineers.

Slide 2 — Matrix explanation (visual will be 3 rows x 3 columns)
Rows (Buyer personas):
  1) Platform / Infra Engineer
  2) Product Manager / Feature Owner
  3) Security & Compliance Lead
Columns (Primary risk areas):
  A) Latency & SLA concerns
  B) Data residency & privacy
  C) Cost predictability & unit economics

Each cell = 4 short pieces: 1-line value prop, 20s demo cue, fallback script (what to promise + immediate fallback), canary metric to measure.

Slide 3 — Matrix contents (exportable copy)
Row 1: Platform / Infra Engineer
  A) Latency & SLA
    - 1-line: "Redwood routes to local model variants + autoscaling pools to hit p99 latency targets — you control fallbacks."
    - 20s demo cue: Live trace showing p50/p95/p99 for stream vs batch (use demo project: demo-slo-traces).
    - Fallback script: "If we miss SLO, automatic downgrade to compact quantized variant and region failover — transparent to app."
    - Canary metric: p99 latency under 95th percentile traffic spike (test: 5m spike with 200RPS).
  B) Data residency & privacy
    - 1-line: "Private control plane + VPC connectors so inference stays inside your network and keys remain customer-managed."
    - 20s demo cue: Show VPC connector config + KMS key binding screenshot.
    - Fallback script: "We can provision a dedicated pool in your VPC or provide an on-prem package for air-gapped runs."
    - Canary metric: No egress logs leaving customer subnets; KMS audit events present.
  C) Cost predictability
    - 1-line: "Reserved Dedicated capacity with burst controls lets you fix unit costs while preserving peak throughput."
    - 20s demo cue: Show cost dashboard for reserved vs burst usage over a week.
    - Fallback script: "Start with a small reserved commit + autoscaling policy; Redwood Optimize will recommend quantization and batching to hit your CPA target."
    - Canary metric: Token/unit cost under target across a 48h pilot window.

Row 2: Product Manager / Feature Owner
  A) Latency & SLA
    - 1-line: "Latency-first routing keeps critical user paths snappy; less important calls can be batched to save cost."
    - 20s demo cue: Short video showing two flows: interactive chat (streaming) vs background summarization (batch).
    - Fallback script: "If latency spikes, we prioritize routing for high-priority routes and shed lower-priority jobs automatically."
    - Canary metric: 90% of interactive requests < target latency during a mixed workload test.
  B) Data residency & privacy
    - 1-line: "You choose what touches Redwood hosted endpoints vs stays on private deployment — consistent API across both."
    - 20s demo cue: Toggle example: switch route from hosted model to private model with zero code changes.
    - Fallback script: "For regulated features, we can pre-provision private model variants to avoid cutover delays."
    - Canary metric: Successful route toggle with no schema drift in 2 test runs.
  C) Cost predictability
    - 1-line: "Predictable inference economics with per-route budgets and automated batching recommendations."
    - 20s demo cue: Show per-route cost burn-down and suggested quantization profile.
    - Fallback script: "Start with a conservative budget; Optimize will surface where we can trade 1% accuracy for 30% cost savings."
    - Canary metric: Feature-level cost per MAU within target in a 7-day window.

Row 3: Security & Compliance Lead
  A) Latency & SLA
    - 1-line: "SLA + audit trails — maintain compliance even when we route to failover models."
    - 20s demo cue: Show audit log schema and redacted request tracing.
    - Fallback script: "If you require, we can route to pre-approved model variants only; all fallbacks are logged and auditable."
    - Canary metric: Audit log entries appear for every fallback event; sampling audit shows no PII leakage.
  B) Data residency & privacy
    - 1-line: "Customer-managed keys, optional on-prem, and configurable retention windows for request/response logs."
    - 20s demo cue: Walk through retention policy UI and KMS rotation entry.
    - Fallback script: "For high-risk flows we suggest private deployment + no persistent logs until approved in design doc."
    - Canary metric: Retention compliance test passes (random sampling).
  C) Cost predictability
    - 1-line: "We can enforce budget guardrails and hard rate limits so billing surprises are eliminated."
    - 20s demo cue: Show rate-limit and quota UI with alerts to Slack/webhook.
    - Fallback script: "Enable hard guardrails in pilot and escalate cap adjustments through the customer success play."
    - Canary metric: No billing alert spikes during pilot; quota hits observed and handled per SLA.

Slide 4 — 60s seller scripts (copyable)
- Platform Engineer opener (30s): "We treat inference like any other infra service — consistent SLAs, dedicated pools, and clear fallbacks. Can I confirm your p99 target?"
- Product PM opener (30s): "We will preserve UX-critical latency while letting you batch low-priority work; what's your highest frequency user flow?"
- Security opener (30s): "We can run in your VPC or hand you the keys — how strict is your retention policy?"

Slide 5 — Pilot acceptance & canary checklist (handout)
- Basic: endpoint response schema, route mapping, and sample load generator wiring.
- Ops canary tests (minimal): 1) ramp to 50% of expected peak for 10m; 2) 5m p99 spike test; 3) route toggle test between hosted and private model with no errors.
- Success thresholds: p95 < target, no loss of request schema, cost under provisional budget.
- Post-pilot artifact: capture traces + Optimize recommendations doc.

Slide 6 — Common objections & suggested rebuttals (quick bullets)
- "We can't trust a hosted provider with our data." -> "We offer private deployment + customer-managed KMS and an on-prem package. Let's scope which flows need that."
- "Costs balloon in production." -> "Start with reserved capacity + Optimize recommendations; we run a pre-mortem cost simulation for you."
- "Latency spikes during batch windows." -> "We segregate latency-critical routes and apply strict scheduling policies; we can demo with your data shape."

Slide 7 — Quick demo checklist for SE (before call)
- Load the demo traces dashboard (demo-slo-traces).
- Have two models ready: hosted-compact and private-standard for toggle demo.
- Prep a 3-step canary run using the included script: scripts/canary-run.sh (note: update RPS variable).

Slide 8 — Implementation notes (internal)
- Keep the demo infra minimal; avoid customer-specific keys in public screens.
- TODO: bake automated route-toggle snippet into demo repo.
- TODO: create short GIFs for each cell to embed in slide handout.
- Question: can we expose a synthetic cost simulator endpoint for sellers? (JIRA:GT-1428)

Slide 9 — Next steps & distribution plan
- Action: run playtest with 3 SEs next week, collect feedback, iterate to 2-slide pocket reference per persona.
- Ask: Product to confirm exact canary script commands and default thresholds.
- Distribution: Google Drive + Slack #se-enablement + Confluence appendix.

Notes to self: keep language short, heavy on action cues and metrics. Avoid deep architecture diagrams in the pocket card — keep them on the technical appendix.

Unresolved (capture in ticket):
- Which exact demo datasets are GDPR/CCPA-safe for public screens?
- Can SRE automate the canary script from CI?

End.
